speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin our evaluation, how old are you and exactly how long has the swelling been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA).

The patient is an 18-month-old boy with a 1-month history of right knee swelling following minor trauma, but with no significant injury. The family history of a similar condition on the maternal side suggests a genetic predisposition. Given the age of onset, monoarticular presentation, and lack of clear traumatic cause, the differential includes transient synovitis, septic arthritis, and JIA. However, the familial component points more strongly towards a genetic etiology like JIA or a metabolic disorder.

To confirm, I will need to review blood work and imaging.
REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, RF, ANA.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Knee_XRay, Right_Knee_Ultrasound.
